title: DMT keeps oxygen-deprived neurons alive via the sigma-1 receptor

tellings.quote: >> Um what's interesting is that in a oxygen hypoxic oxygend deprived environment um neurons will survive longer in the presence of DMT.

plain: DMT, a powerful psychedelic compound, may help brain cells survive when they are starved of oxygen, according to the neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore. He tells Michels, without citing a particular study, that "neurons will survive longer in the presence of DMT" in an oxygen-deprived setting, an effect that the story links to the sigma-1 receptor, a protein on cells that DMT binds to. If true, it would mean the compound protects the brain as well as altering the mind.
